subject: Mutual action plan: cost sensitivity, eval milestones, and batching assumptions
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Ellis <nora.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action plan: cost sensitivity, eval milestones, and batching assumptions

Hi Nora —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together a short Mutual Action Plan focused on the cost side of the evaluation so your finance and infra teams can sign off quickly. Primary goals: confirm tokens/$ under your workload, validate caching and batching assumptions, and get a short evaluation run that maps to production traffic.

High-level ask for Acme:
- Share a redacted sample of the prompt mix (top 15 prompt templates + avg input length) — this lets us size KV cache benefit.
- Confirm desired SLOs (p95 latency target) and monthly token budget for evaluation.
- Approve a week-long canary that uses your production-ish traffic routing so we can validate batching behavior.

Our commitments from Redwood:
- Deliver a cost model spreadsheet (attached) with: tokens/sec, tokens/$, cache-hit sensitivity (10/30/50%), and batching scenarios (batch sizes 1/4/16).
- Instrument evaluation with token-level usage and per-route latency breakdown; share daily reports.
- If the cost model is off by >20% during the canary, we’ll run a quick tuning pass (adjust batching, suggest quantization profile) at no additional charge.

Timeline proposal:
- Tue 5/18: Exchange sample prompts and fill evaluation onboarding form.
- Wed 5/19: Redwood sends updated cost model (first-pass) and proposed canary config.
- Thu 5/20 — Thu 5/27: Canary (7 days) + daily check-ins.
- Fri 5/28: Final cost sign-off and commercial close.

I attached the draft MAP and the cost model. I put conservative defaults in the sheet (20% cache hit, batching = 4). If you have internal throughput numbers we can swap those in.

Can you confirm the sample prompt export and budget by EOD tomorrow so we can stick to this timeline?

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 (415) 555-0189

Attachments: ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), inference-cost-model-v2.pdf (summary)

From: Nora Ellis <nora.ellis@acme.com>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: cost sensitivity, eval milestones, and batching assumptions

Thanks, Evelyn — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side before we share the prompt export: 

1) When you say "tokens/$" in the sheet, is that pre- or post-caching? We need the effective cost after cache 
2) Our infra team is sensitive to batching that increases tail latency. Can you confirm whether your default batching of 4 impacts p95?
3) For the canary, we can allocate 300k tokens/day for the first 3 days and then scale to 1.2M/day for the remainder, is that sufficient?

We can provide the redacted prompt list by EOD tomorrow. Also loop in Marissa from CS — she’ll own the day-to-day during the canary.

Best,
Nora
Nora Ellis
VP Product, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: cost sensitivity, eval milestones, and batching assumptions

Nora —

Great questions; answers below and I updated the attached cost model with an "effective cost" tab that folds caching into tokens/$.

1) tokens/$: the sheet shows both raw (no cache) and effective (cache-hit adjusted) rates. We model cache-hit sensitivities at 10%, 30%, and 50% — the effective tokens/$ row is a weighted average accordingly.

2) batching vs p95: our serving runtime uses continuous batching with latency-aware thresholds. Default batch=4 is our middle ground; for your p95-sensitive routes we can set max-batch-time to 15ms which keeps p95 impact <5% in our internal tests. I added a short microbenchmark in the sheet showing p50/p95 at batch sizes 1/4/16 under 3 sequence-length distributions.

3) canary token budget: 300k/day to start then 1.2M/day is plenty to capture steady-state behavior for the features you care about. We’ll instrument per-route token split so we can simulate production mix.

Next steps:
- I attached ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx (now with effective-cost tab) — please review.
- Marissa, could you own the day-to-day check-ins and the daily report cadence?

If that all looks good we’ll provision the canary cluster and share a runbook.

Cheers,
Evelyn

Attachments: ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx, inference-cost-model-v2.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Ellis <nora.ellis@acme.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: cost sensitivity, eval milestones, and batching assumptions

Nora —

I’ll take day-to-day on this. Quick notes on what we'll send during the canary: 
- Daily token usage and cost burn-down (CSV).
- Per-route latency heatmap (p50/p95/p99).
- A short run-of-show for the 7-day canary (deploy timeline + rollback triggers).

We also recommend the following acceptance criteria for cost sign-off (so procurement has clear gates):
- Observed effective tokens/$ within ±15% of the model for the last 3 days of the canary.
- No route with p95 > your target for more than 30 minutes total during the canary.
- No more than 2 incidents requiring manual rollback.

I’ll attach the runbook to the shared Drive link once Evelyn provisions the cluster.

—Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
